PipelineDB allows you to define continuous SQL queries that perpetually aggregate time-series data and store **only the aggregate output** in regular, queryable tables. You can think of this concept as extremely high-throughput, incrementally updated materialized views that never need to be manually refreshed.
Continuous queries produce their own output streams, and thus can be chained together into arbitrary networks of continuous SQL.
If you just want to start using PipelineDB right away, head over to the installation docs to get going.
Since PipelineDB is a PostgreSQL extension, you'll need to have the PostgreSQL development packages installed to build PipelineDB.
Next you'll have to install ZeroMQ which PipelineDB uses for inter-process communication. Here's a gist with instructions to build and install ZeroMQ from source.
=# CREATE FOREIGN TABLE test_stream (key integer, value integer) SERVER pipelinedb;
=# CREATE VIEW test_view WITH (action=materialize) AS SELECT key, COUNT(*) FROM test_stream GROUP BY key;
=# INSERT INTO test_stream (key, value) SELECT random() * 10, random() * 10 FROM generate_series(1, 100000);
$ psql -c "SELECT * FROM test_view ORDER BY count DESC limit 10"

Built by the community and William & Mary geoLab, the geoBoundaries Global Database of Political Administrative Boundaries Database is an online, open license (CC BY 4.0 / ODbL) resource of information on administrative boundaries (i.e., state, county) for every country in the world. Since 2016, we have tracked approximately 1 million boundaries within over 200 entities, including all UN member states. All boundaries are available to view or download in common file formats; the only requirement for use is acknowledgement.

The geoBoundaries project is made up of a number of different repositories; you are currently on the core repo which stores all input datasets and builds. If you are interested in understanding other components of geoBoundaries, you can visit:

- geoBoundaryBot: where our build scripts live, as well as the various QA/QC algorithms applied to pull requests in this repository. If you're interested in the specifics of our topology checks or simplification strategies, this is where to look.
- gbWeb: where the website itself lives, as well as the API. Various scripts that aid in building the API and other things related to the website can be found here as well.
- rgeoboundaries: built by community member @dickoa, this library allows you to retrieve and manipulate geoBoundaries data within the R programming environment.
- pygeoboundaries built by community member @ibhalin, this package allows you to retrieve and manipulate geoBoundaries data within the python programming environment.

We welcome contributions to the geoBoundaries dataset. Involvement can take many forms: assistance identifying errors in the database, contributing boundary files, or even contributing code for our build or website scripts. To get started, you could:

- Report Boundary Errors: While we try to ensure geoBoundaries is as error-free as possible, we are currently tracking around 300 million vertices across hundreds-of-thousands of geometries - there are bound to be issues! We very much welcome any reports of errors across the database.

- Contribute Boundaries: We carefully curate all boundaries that are submitted to the database, and have a very active community. Join us in the fun! We try to keep things simple for everyone, requiring only a zipfile upload.
- Fix Known Issues: We have a number of known issues with the database, and always welcome contributions that might fix any of these.

- Help with the Python Code: We always welcome contributions to our codebase that improve the efficiency of our processing, or introduce new types of checks to automatically prevent errors. Our code includes a number of different pieces, such as the www.geoboundaries.org website, API, the geoBoundaryBot (responds to PRs), and our formal build scripts.

We provide three different mechanisms to download geoBoundaries data: a web-based GUI, HTML file access on GitHub (for archival versions), and an API. Releases come in both unsimplified and simplified types, and include a global composite of ADM0, ADM1, and ADM2 with gaps filled between borders ("CGAZ"). Acronyms describing these datasets you may encounter include:

_HPSC_ - High Precision Single Country. The premier geoBoundaries release, representing the highest precision files available for every country in the world. Every country is represented as that country represents itself, so (for example) two countries may overlap in the case of contested boundaries.
_SSC_ - Simplified Single Country. A simplified version of every file available for every country in the world, using the HPSCU product as a base.

_CGAZ_ - Comprehensive Global Administrative Zones. A global composite of the SSC ADM0, ADM1 and ADM2, clipped to international boundaries (US Department of State), with gaps filled between borders. Also available at higher levels of simplification.

- **Hybrid search** -- Reciprocal Rank Fusion (Cormack, Clarke & Butt, SIGIR 2009) combining dense vector similarity (pgvector) with BM25-style keyword matching (PostgreSQL tsvector). Two independent retrieval systems, rank-fused without score normalisation.

- **Entity overlap boost** -- memories sharing named entities with the query receive a bounded relevance boost (up to 1.4x), inspired by entity-linking literature (Kolitsas et al., CoNLL 2018). Entity extraction covers 18 languages via YAML-based word lists with no LLM in the write path.

- **Matryoshka embeddings** -- flexible dimensionality via Matryoshka Representation Learning (Kusupati et al., NeurIPS 2022). Embedding providers (OpenAI, Voyage, Gemini, Ollama) produce native-dimension vectors truncated to 512d, enabling provider-portable storage without re-embedding.

- **Temporal diversity re-ranking** -- density-gated soft penalty preventing semantic clustering on a single time period, extending Maximal Marginal Relevance principles (Carbonell & Goldstein, SIGIR 1998). Only activates when the top-k results are temporally concentrated, leaving well-distributed results untouched.

- **ACT-R importance scoring** -- cognitive-architecture-inspired memory weighting based on recency, access frequency, and surprise (Anderson & Lebiere, 1998). Frequently accessed memories stay sharp, rarely accessed ones fade, disputed ones drop in ranking without deletion.

- **Hebbian decay and potentiation** -- memories that are not accessed lose importance over time (5% per 30-day idle period). Memories accessed 10+ times become "potentiated" with a slower decay rate (1% per 30 days), simulating long-term potentiation. Based on Hebb's learning rule (Hebb, 1949) and computational models of synaptic plasticity (Bi & Poo, 2001). Importance serves as a multiplier in the relevance formula -- decayed memories sink in rankings but remain retrievable (floor at 0.05). Original importance is preserved in metadata for recovery. Run as a batch job via `ogham decay` or pg_cron.

The project **SQLite3 Multiple Ciphers** implements an encryption extension for SQLite with support for multiple ciphers. In the past the encryption extension was bundled with the project wxSQLite3, which provides a thin SQLite3 database wrapper for wxWidgets.

In the course of time several developers had asked for a stand-alone version of the _wxSQLite3 encryption extension_. Originally it was planned to undertake the separation process already in 2019, but due to personal matters it had to be postponed for several months. However, maybe that wasn't that bad after all, because there were changes to the public SQLite code on Feb 7, 2020: “Simplify the code by removing the unsupported and undocumented SQLITE_HAS_CODEC compile-time option”. These changes took effect with the release of SQLite version 3.32.0 on May 22, 2020. As a consequence, all SQLite encryption extensions out there will not be able to easily support SQLite version 3.32.0 and later.

In late February 2020 work started on a new implementation of a SQLite encryption extension that will be able to support SQLite 3.32.0 and later. The new approach is based on SQLite's VFS feature. This approach has its pros and cons. On the one hand, the code is less closely coupled with SQLite itself; on the other hand, access to SQLite's internal data structures is more complex.

有副机时**先升副机,再升主机**:主机用到新功能后,版本不够的副机会整份拒收同步、按旧配置继续服务,直到它升级;主机容灾的备用比主机旧时保留名次,但收不到新的数据副本。面板、代理面板或外部 API 挂在反向代理(Nginx、Caddy 等)后面的:v0.7.17 起外部 API 令牌错 10 次会暂停这个来源 5 分钟(面板登录本来就有),不设的话所有请求的来源都是反代自己,一个人连错就把大家一起挡住,升级后到 设置 → 面板 → **受信任的反向代理** 填上反代的地址(同机反代填 `127.0.0.1, ::1`,见 docs/API.md)。升级到 v0.7.17 后**主机容灾默认关闭**,要用就在主机的 设置 → 主机容灾 里打开(见主机容灾与设为主机);不打开时一切照旧。另外 v0.7.17 起 sing-box 订阅也按线路出测速组,外部订阅里和线路同名的节点改叫「X 2」,客户端里选着它的用户要重新选一次(见外部节点)。

- 公告与联系方式里可以写链接:`文字(https://…)` 或 `文字` 在页面上只显示文字,括号、方括号半角全角都行(中文输入法打出来的 `【文字】（链接）` 也认)。`文字(链接)` 的括号前空一格也行;链接文字从括号往前取,到最近的标点、上一个链接或前面自动识别出的地址 / @用户名 / 号码为止。`Tg: @用户名`(Telegram、电报、飞机同样,前面紧挨着汉字也认)和 `WhatsApp: +号码`(WA、WS 同样)会自动变成可点的链接;裸写的 `https://…` 地址本身就是链接。只认 http(s)、tg、mailto、tel 链接,别的照原样显示成文字;字号不变。文字里有 `/`、或链接里有括号时用 `文字`。
API 地址是 `http://` 时,令牌与全部用户凭据明文过公网(服务器页标「明文」):建议副机面板开 HTTPS(自签即可),或让副机端口只对主机开放。

**大陆连通检测**:服务器页的「大陆连通」一列,由主机借 Globalping 公共测试网络,从大陆移动、电信、联通的家庭宽带测点(不含机房测点)连每台服务器,香港测点作对照。大陆三网都连不上、香港能连 → 判为被墙;再补测一次 ping,分清是整个 IP 被墙(换 IP)还是只有端口被封(换端口)。测的是这台服务器上订阅里走 IPv4 的第一条 TCP 线路的端口(走 IPv6 的线路——包括自定义地址写成这台自己 IPv6 的——不拿来测 IPv4 地址;自定义地址是国内中转、CDN 之类别处的 IPv6 时,用户连的是中转,线路端口照样拿来测这台的 IPv4);走 IPv4 的只有 hysteria2 / tuic 这类 UDP 线路时测订阅或面板端口,只能看出 IP 有没有被墙,面板端口只对主机放行、香港测点也连不上时记"无可测端口"(灰色、不告警);副机的线路在订阅里都走 IPv6 时这一项不测,同样记"无可测端口",以前测出的结论不再挂着;主机照测订阅地址的 IPv4 和订阅端口——用户刷新订阅连的是订阅地址,它的 IPv4 被墙时大陆用户拿不到新节点;订阅地址是域名时在主机上解析,测解析出来的 IPv4——订阅地址本身是 IPv6、或是没有 A 记录(只有 AAAA)的域名时才记"无可测端口"。服务器根本没有 IPv4(只上报了 IPv6,连接地址、域名也解析不到 IPv4)时,线路走中转、订阅给域名也一样记"无可测端口",主机副机都是;解析域名出错(超时之类,不是没有记录)时算没测成。只测 IPv4 是因为大陆的家庭宽带测点大多没有 IPv6,拿它们测 IPv6 会把正常的服务器误判成被墙。可手动检测,也会定时巡检(默认每 90 分钟,**设置 → 大陆连通检测**里可改或关闭),发现异常先隔两分钟复测,仍异常才发 Telegram,恢复时再通知。检测时服务器地址会发给 Globalping;免登录额度每小时约 250 个测点次(测一台约 15 个,有走 IPv6 的线路的再加约 4 个;额度先保大陆检测),填免费令牌可提高。
- **写操作暂停多久**:通常一两分钟;最长按库的大小算(15–60 分钟),进度框和页面顶部写着截止时间。暂停期间面板只读,外部 API、代理面板、Telegram 机器人和订阅页的临时共享返回 503,对接的程序要能重试。

- **失败与结果不明**:提交之前任何一步失败(包括传得太慢、快到截止),都会自动取消、恢复写操作,数据不变。提交请求发出后没收到回话时,结果算「不明」:写操作继续暂停,原主机每 10 秒问一次那台;到截止还没结论(或你在进度框里点「放弃(隔离目标)」并再输一次密码),原主机先再问一次那台、看各副机跟的是谁:已经有副机跟了那台,就按换主机完成;否则以更高的纪元继续当主机、恢复写操作,那台之后就算起来,副机也不认它,它会自动变为副机,它那份数据不生效。隔离要副机确认收到撤销才做:截止前放弃要那台以外的副机全部确认,截止后过半即可;确认不够时写操作继续暂停,连不上的副机恢复后自动完成。
- **流量**:交接期间两台自己线路上的流量照常计费。原主机从暂停写操作起另记一本账(同时照常记进用户用量),整库数据里带着这本账同一时刻的计数;它变为副机后接着这本账上报,新主机只收打包之后的那段。那台收到数据之后到重启之间自己记的,换上新库时并进去。其它副机线路上的流量照常按游标补回。没做成时原主机照旧当主机,另记的那本账丢掉,用量不受影响。
- **全新 VPS 当主机**:照常装好 m-ui,作为副机加进来(和加普通副机一样),同步上以后对它「设为主机」。用明文 http 连的服务器要在确认框里勾选风险确认(「我知道和它的链接是明文 http:……仍要继续」)才能设为主机:明文链接上的主动中间人能拿到并改写整库,建议先换成 https(自签证书 + 指纹即可)。

- **订阅地址不变**:订阅的域名、端口、路径和订阅证书随主机身份一起迁过去(订阅端口按客户端请求的域名挑证书,本机原来的证书照样给本机自己的域名用);把订阅域名的 DNS 指到新主机后,用户手里的订阅地址照常能用。订阅地址用的是 IP、或迁过去的订阅端口和那台的面板 / 代理面板 / WARP 端口或线路端口冲突时,那台继续用自己的订阅端口,订阅地址会变,确认框里会提前说。面板、代理面板用新主机自己的地址。
